questions.question: One root of the quadratic equation 2x² + (k + 3)x + 2k = 0 is the reciprocal of the other. Find the roots.
questions.questionHtml: One root of the quadratic equation 2x² + (k + 3)x + 2k = 0 is the reciprocal of the other. Find the roots.
questions.solution:
2x² + (k + 3)x + 2k = 0

If one root is the reciprocal of the other, then

Product of roots = 1

But product of roots = c/a = 2k/2 = k

So, k = 1

Substitute k = 1:

2x² + 4x + 2 = 0

Divide by 2:

x² + 2x + 1 = 0

(x + 1)² = 0

Roots = −1, −1

questions.question: The roots of the equation ax3−24x2+188x−480=0 are three consecutive even natural numbers. The value of a is:
questions.questionHtml: The roots of the equation ax3−24x2+188x−480=0 are three consecutive even natural numbers. The value of a is:
questions.solution:
Roots are three consecutive even numbers:
n − 2, n, n + 2

For equation
ax³ − 24x² + 188x − 480 = 0

Sum of roots:

(n−2) + n + (n+2) = 24/a
3n = 24/a → n = 8/a

Sum of product of roots:

(n−2)n + n(n+2) + (n−2)(n+2) = 188/a
3n² − 4 = 188/a

Put n = 8/a

192/a² − 4 = 188/a

4a² + 188a − 192 = 0

a² + 47a − 48 = 0

(a + 48)(a − 1) = 0

Since roots are natural numbers,

a = 1

questions.question: Water is flowing through a cylindrical pipe of diameter 6 mm at the rate of 10 m/min. How much time will it take to fill a conical vessel whose base diameter is 60 cm and depth is 21 cm?
questions.questionHtml: Water is flowing through a cylindrical pipe of diameter 6 mm at the rate of 10 m/min. How much time will it take to fill a conical vessel whose base diameter is 60 cm and depth is 21 cm?
questions.solution:
Pipe diameter = 6 mm = 0.6 cm → r = 0.3 cm
Speed = 10 m/min = 1000 cm/min

Water per minute
= πr²h
= π × (0.3)² × 1000
= 90π

Cone: r = 30 cm, h = 21 cm

Volume
= (1/3)πr²h
= (1/3)π × 30² × 21
= 6300π

Time
= 6300π / 90π
= 70 minutes

=1 hr, 10 min

questions.question: Three persons A, B and C took part in a race of 2000 m. At the same time, to reach the finish line, A can give B a start of 500 m and C a start of 300 m. In a race of 3400 m, how many metres start can C give to B?
questions.questionHtml: Three persons A, B and C took part in a race of 2000 m. At the same time, to reach the finish line, A can give B a start of 500 m and C a start of 300 m. In a race of 3400 m, how many metres start can C give to B?
questions.solution:
Race = 2000 m

When A finishes:
B covers = 2000 − 500 = 1500 m
C covers = 2000 − 300 = 1700 m

Speed ratio B : C = 1500 : 1700 = 15 : 17

In 3400 m race, B covers = (15/17) × 3400 = 3000 m

Start C can give B = 3400 − 3000 = 400 m

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 86% of the registered voters cast their votes and 6% of the votes polled were declared invalid. The winning candidate got 58% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 202100 votes. How many voters were registered?
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, 86% of the registered voters cast their votes and 6% of the votes polled were declared invalid. The winning candidate got 58% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 202100 votes. How many voters were registered?
questions.solution:
Let the total number of registered voters = x

Winning candidate’s votes = 58% of valid votes
Losing candidate’s votes = 42% of valid votes

Vote margin = 58% − 42% = 16% of valid votes = 0.16 × 0.8084x = 0.129344x

Given margin = 202,100

0.129344x = 202,100 → x = 202,100/0.129344

x = 1,562,500
